es: Repasar cómo el tono, el registro y lo implícito (indirectas, sarcasmo, falsos elogios) cambian el significado de un mensaje, e interpretar mensajes breves más allá de sus palabras.

vocabulary.es: tomar al pie de la letra

teaching.en: Her warm tone made the bad news easier to hear, while his frosty reply, although polite, made the same news feel like a complaint.
teaching.es: Su tono cordial hizo más fácil oír la mala noticia, mientras que su respuesta gélida, aunque cortés, hizo que la misma noticia pareciera una queja.
teaching.explanationEs: El tono es la actitud del mensaje: warm suaviza; frosty (muy frío) endurece aunque las palabras sean corteses.
segments: Her warm tone made the bad news easier to hear, while his
frosty reply, although polite, made the same news feel like a complaint.
teaching.audioText: Her warm tone made the bad news easier to hear, while his frosty reply, although polite, made the same news feel like a complaint.

teaching.en: “Wow, what lovely weather,” he said in a flat voice, and everyone understood that he was being sarcastic about the rain.
teaching.es: «Vaya, qué buen tiempo», dijo con voz plana, y todos entendieron que era sarcástico con la lluvia.
teaching.explanationEs: Sarcasmo: las palabras son positivas, pero el sentido es el contrario; la voz plana y el contexto lo delatan.
segments: “Wow, what lovely weather,” he said in a flat voice, and
everyone understood that he was being sarcastic about the rain.
teaching.audioText: “Wow, what lovely weather,” he said in a flat voice, and everyone understood that he was being sarcastic about the rain.

teaching.en: I would be grateful if you could confirm the date by Friday, which sounds polite because the register is formal.
teaching.es: Le agradecería que pudiera confirmar la fecha antes del viernes, lo cual suena cortés porque el registro es formal.
teaching.explanationEs: Registro formal: would be grateful if you could + verbo base, sin contracciones.
segments: I would be grateful if you could confirm the date
by Friday, which sounds polite because the register is formal.
teaching.audioText: I would be grateful if you could confirm the date by Friday, which sounds polite because the register is formal.

teaching.en: She dropped a hint rather than a request: “It's a bit cold in here,” which a tactful listener understands as a wish to close the window.
teaching.es: Dejó caer una indirecta en vez de una petición: «Hace un poco de frío aquí», que un oyente con tacto entiende como un deseo de cerrar la ventana.
teaching.explanationEs: Indirecta: la frase describe un hecho, pero pide una acción; tactful = atento a cómo se dicen las cosas.
segments: She dropped a hint rather than a request: “It's a bit cold in
here,” which a tactful listener understands as a wish to close the window.
teaching.audioText: She dropped a hint rather than a request: “It's a bit cold in here,” which a tactful listener understands as a wish to close the window.

teaching.en: With friends we use a casual register, but with a manager we use a more formal one, so the same request can sound very different.
teaching.es: Con amigos usamos un registro informal, pero con un jefe usamos uno más formal, así que la misma petición puede sonar muy distinta.
teaching.explanationEs: Registro: nivel de formalidad. Hey, can you…? con amigos; I was wondering if… con un jefe.
segments: With friends we use a casual register, but with a manager we use
a more formal one, so the same request can sound very different.
teaching.audioText: With friends we use a casual register, but with a manager we use a more formal one, so the same request can sound very different.

teaching.en: A backhanded compliment sounds kind, but we should not take at face value any praise that is too effusive or carries a hidden criticism in its tone.
teaching.es: Un elogio con doble intención suena amable, pero no debemos tomar al pie de la letra un halago demasiado efusivo o que lleva una crítica escondida en el tono.
teaching.explanationEs: Backhanded compliment: elogio que critica; effusive = exagerado en el elogio; take at face value = creer solo lo que dicen las palabras.
segments: A backhanded compliment sounds kind, but we should not take at face value any
praise that is too effusive or carries a hidden criticism in its tone.
teaching.audioText: A backhanded compliment sounds kind, but we should not take at face value any praise that is too effusive or carries a hidden criticism in its tone.

prompt.es: Elige cómo hay que interpretar el mensaje de Sara.

choices.text: She is being warm: she is pleased to have extra time.
She is being sarcastic: the praise hides that she is annoyed.
She is being formal: she is reporting a timetable fact.

feedback.es: Las palabras son positivas, pero la situación (perdió el autobús, como siempre) muestra molestia: es sarcasmo.

hint.es: Compara la palabra «great» con lo que acaba de pasarle a Sara.

origin.text: Sara misses the bus and texts her friend: “Wow, great timing. The bus left two minutes ago, as usual.”

prompt.es: Completa: «No lo tomé al pie de la letra, porque sonaba a indirecta.»

answer.text: face

feedback.es: Take at face value significa creer solo lo que dicen las palabras, sin mirar el tono ni la intención.

hint.es: Es la palabra que va entre «at» y «value»: significa «cara».

origin.text: I was not sure whether her comment was praise or criticism, so I did not take it at ___ value.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Le agradecería que pudiera confirmar la fecha hoy.»

answer.text: I would be grateful if you could confirm the date today

feedback.es: Would be grateful if you could + verbo base es la fórmula formal para pedir un favor con cortesía.

hint.es: Empieza con I would be grateful.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo interpreta la narradora el comentario de Marta.

choices.text: As a joke that Marta meant everyone to enjoy.
As a sincere but blunt attempt to encourage her.
As praise that hides doubt about her ability.

feedback.es: El tono plano y «surprisingly» revelan que Marta dudaba de ella: el elogio esconde una crítica; no era una broma ni un aliento sincero aunque brusco.

origin.audio: At the office party, my colleague Marta told me that my presentation was surprisingly good. She smiled, but her voice was flat, and she added that she had expected much worse. Everyone around us laughed, so I laughed too, although I felt worried. On the way home I realised that her comment was a backhanded compliment: the words praised me, but the tone and the word surprisingly suggested that she had doubted my ability all along.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada mensaje con lo que transmite.

pairs: Hey, got the file?
I would be grateful if you could reply.
Brilliant. The lift is broken again.
It's a bit cold in here.

feedback.es: Cada mensaje tiene una pista: hey marca lo informal, would be grateful lo formal, brilliant más un problema el sarcasmo y el dato del frío una indirecta.

pairs: Hey, got the file?
I would be grateful if you could reply.
Brilliant. The lift is broken again.
It's a bit cold in here.

prompt.es: Elige el mensaje más adecuado para pedir una reunión a tu profesora.

choices.text: Dear Ms Lopez, I would be grateful if we could meet on Friday.
Hi Ms Lopez, could we meet on Friday afternoon? Cheers, and thanks so much!
Ms Lopez, meet me on Friday at three.

feedback.es: Con una profesora se usa un registro formal; la opción amistosa con Cheers resulta demasiado informal y la orden directa suena brusca.

origin.text: You want to ask your teacher for a meeting. Her last email to the class was formal and very brief.

prompt.es: ¿Qué quiere dar a entender realmente la directora en su correo?

choices.text: That she is unhappy and wants to start the draft again.
That the draft needs more examples before Friday.
That she will rewrite the draft herself on Friday.

feedback.es: Tras el elogio, «I would have preferred a few more examples» es una crítica suavizada: pide añadir ejemplos antes del viernes, no rehacerlo todo.

origin.text: Manager's email: “Thanks for the draft. It is clear that you have worked hard. I would have preferred a few more examples, but I am sure we can sort that out before Friday.”

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué quiere decir en realidad el vecino.

choices.text: That he likes my music and wants to hear more.
That he is only asking about the building's rules.
That he wants the music turned down.

feedback.es: El elogio sonriente y la pregunta sobre las horas de silencio forman una indirecta: pide bajar la música sin decirlo.

origin.audio: My neighbour came to the door at ten o'clock and said, with a wide smile, that some people's music was really lovely at night. Then he asked whether I had seen the new notice about quiet hours in the building.

prompt.es: Completa: «Fue una respuesta muy brusca, sin saludo y sin motivo.»

answer.text: blunt

feedback.es: Una respuesta de una sola palabra, sin saludo ni please, es seca: blunt describe ese tono.

origin.text: He only wrote “No.” It was a very ___ reply, with no greeting, no please and no reason.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Su tono era cordial, pero sus palabras eran muy directas.»

answer.text: His tone was warm but his words were blunt
accepted: His tone was warm but his words were blunt
His words were blunt but his tone was warm

feedback.es: El contraste entre tono y palabras es clave: un tono cordial puede acompañar un contenido muy directo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sugiere realmente el comentario de la colega?

choices.text: That she thinks he prepared too little.
That she respects his calm under pressure.
That she wants him to prepare the next meeting.

feedback.es: Elogiar la calma «about preparation» es un elogio con doble intención: sugiere que preparó poco.

origin.text: A colleague sends you this message after a meeting: “Thanks for stepping in today. It is rare to see someone so relaxed about preparation.”

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué ilustra el ejemplo de la narradora.

choices.text: That formal messages are always longer and warmer than casual ones.
That register shifts with the reader, though the content is the same.
That a polite tone matters less than the information given.

feedback.es: Las dos respuestas dicen que sí, pero el registro cambia según el lector: informal con el amigo y formal con la directora.

origin.audio: I wrote two replies to the same invitation. To my friend I wrote, hey, count me in, see you there. To my director I wrote, dear Ms Clark, thank you for the invitation, and I would be happy to attend. Both messages say yes, but the choice of words changes how each one sounds.

prompt.es: Completa: «Con mi jefa uso un registro más formal que con mis amigos.»

answer.text: register

feedback.es: Register es el nivel de formalidad: cambia según la persona con la que hablas.

origin.text: I use a more formal ___ with my boss than with my friends, and I avoid contractions in my emails to her.

es: Repasar en un mismo ejercicio los tags, la deducción (must have / can't have), wish, las oraciones enfáticas y la cautela académica, corregir frases con errores de cada forma e interpretar qué postura expresa cada una.

teaching.en: You forgot the tickets again, didn't you? I told you twice that the concert starts at eight, so I expected you to bring them.
teaching.es: Olvidaste otra vez las entradas, ¿verdad? Te dije dos veces que el concierto empieza a las ocho, así que esperaba que las trajeras.
teaching.explanationEs: Tag: el auxiliar cambia de polaridad (forgot → didn't you) y aquí reprocha, no pregunta.
segments: You forgot the tickets again, didn't you? I told you twice that
the concert starts at eight, so I expected you to bring them.
teaching.audioText: You forgot the tickets again, didn't you? I told you twice that the concert starts at eight, so I expected you to bring them.

teaching.en: He must have missed the bus, because he is never late, and he can't have forgotten the meeting, since he wrote the agenda himself.
teaching.es: Debe de haber perdido el autobús, porque nunca llega tarde, y no puede haberse olvidado de la reunión, ya que escribió él mismo el orden del día.
teaching.explanationEs: must have + participio: deducción casi segura; can't have + participio: deducción de que algo es imposible.
segments: He must have missed the bus, because he is never late, and
he can't have forgotten the meeting, since he wrote the agenda himself.
teaching.audioText: He must have missed the bus, because he is never late, and he can't have forgotten the meeting, since he wrote the agenda himself.

teaching.en: I wish I had more time for my holiday, and I wish I had listened to my sister, who told me to book the flights earlier.
teaching.es: Ojalá tuviera más tiempo para mis vacaciones, y ojalá hubiera escuchado a mi hermana, que me dijo que reservara los vuelos antes.
teaching.explanationEs: wish + pasado simple: presente irreal; wish + had + participio: lamento por algo que pasó. Con would se expresa una queja: I wish you would stop.
segments: I wish I had more time for my holiday, and I wish I
had listened to my sister, who told me to book the flights earlier.
teaching.audioText: I wish I had more time for my holiday, and I wish I had listened to my sister, who told me to book the flights earlier.

teaching.en: It was Tom who broke the window, not Leo, and what I need is an honest explanation from him, not more excuses.
teaching.es: Fue Tom quien rompió la ventana, no Leo, y lo que necesito es una explicación sincera de él, no más excusas.
teaching.explanationEs: It was + persona + who/that y What I need is + nombre: dos formas de enfatizar qué o quién.
segments: It was Tom who broke the window, not Leo, and what
I need is an honest explanation from him, not more excuses.
teaching.audioText: It was Tom who broke the window, not Leo, and what I need is an honest explanation from him, not more excuses.

teaching.en: The findings may indicate that sleep helps memory, but it could be argued that the current findings are far from complete.
teaching.es: Los hallazgos pueden indicar que dormir ayuda a la memoria, pero se podría sostener que los resultados actuales están lejos de ser completos.
teaching.explanationEs: Cautela académica: may indicate y it could be argued that suavizan la afirmación.
segments: The findings may indicate that sleep helps memory, but it could
be argued that the current findings are far from complete.
teaching.audioText: The findings may indicate that sleep helps memory, but it could be argued that the current findings are far from complete.

teaching.en: Although the findings look encouraging, there is no conclusive evidence yet, so the authors speak of a possible link rather than a proven cause.
teaching.es: Aunque los resultados parecen alentadores, todavía no hay pruebas concluyentes, así que los autores hablan de un posible vínculo y no de una causa demostrada.
teaching.explanationEs: No conclusive evidence: no hay pruebas definitivas; a possible link vs. a proven cause marca la cautela.
segments: Although the findings look encouraging, there is no conclusive evidence yet, so
the authors speak of a possible link rather than a proven cause.
teaching.audioText: Although the findings look encouraging, there is no conclusive evidence yet, so the authors speak of a possible link rather than a proven cause.

prompt.es: Elige la deducción más natural sobre Sara.

choices.text: She must left early to catch her train.
She can't have left early, because she was tired.
She must have left early to catch her train.

feedback.es: Must have + participio (left) expresa una deducción casi segura sobre el pasado; must left no existe y can't have contradice los datos.

hint.es: Fíjate en qué forma verbal va después de must have y en lo que dicen el abrigo y el tren.

origin.text: Nobody saw Sara leave the party, and her coat is gone. Everyone agrees that she was tired and that she had an early train.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ojalá tuviera más tiempo para ayudarlo, pero mi tren sale en diez minutos.»

answer.text: had

feedback.es: Wish + pasado simple (had) expresa un deseo sobre el presente que no es real.

hint.es: Para un deseo sobre el presente, wish va con pasado simple.

origin.text: Tom looks nervous and keeps checking his phone. I wish I ___ more time to help him, but my train leaves in ten minutes.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Olvidaste las llaves otra vez, ¿verdad?»

answer.text: You forgot the keys again didn't you

feedback.es: El tag didn't you cierra una frase afirmativa en pasado con el auxiliar contrario.

hint.es: El tag usa el auxiliar contrario: didn't + you.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la forma de matiz que usa.

pairs: What I need is a quiet weekend with no emails.
He can't have seen us, because the window was closed.
The results may indicate a link between the two.
It's cold in here, isn't it?

feedback.es: Cada frase usa una forma distinta: What I need is… enfatiza, can't have deduce lo imposible, may indicate suaviza y isn't it confirma.

pairs: What I need is a quiet weekend with no emails.
He can't have seen us, because the window was closed.
The results may indicate a link between the two.
It's cold in here, isn't it?

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué lamenta el hermano del narrador.

choices.text: That he did not check the timetable before leaving.
That the sign showed the wrong departure time.
That the narrator insisted on leaving so late.

feedback.es: «He wished he had checked the timetable» es un lamento por algo que no hizo; la queja de que él insistió en salir tarde la hace la narradora.

origin.audio: Last Saturday, my brother and I arrived at the station and found it almost empty. The sign said that the last train had left ten minutes earlier. My brother said that he wished he had checked the timetable before we left, and I replied that it was he who had insisted on leaving late. Then we sat on a bench and laughed about it, because there was nothing else to do.

prompt.es: Elige la versión más cauta de la afirmación de la alumna.

choices.text: Screen time reduces concentration, as many findings indicate.
Screen time may well reduce concentration in some students.
Screen time will certainly reduce concentration in every student.

feedback.es: May well y in some students limitan la afirmación; las otras opciones siguen siendo categóricas, aunque citen estudios o generalicen a todos.

origin.text: A student writes: “Screen time harms concentration.” Her teacher asks her to sound more cautious and more careful.

prompt.es: Elige la versión corregida del mensaje sobre la ventana.

choices.text: You left the window open again, weren't you? I wish you had closed it, because it must have rained all night.
You left the window open again, didn't you? I wish you had closed it, because it must rained all night.
You left the window open again, didn't you? I wish you had closed it, because it must have rained all night.

feedback.es: Hay tres errores que corregir: el tag (didn't you), wish + had + participio para el lamento y must have + participio para la deducción.

origin.text: Draft message: “You left the window open again, isn't it? I wish you would have closed it, because it must rained all night.”

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué deduce la segunda persona y por qué.

choices.text: That Tom can't be the one, because he left an hour earlier.
That Leo must be guilty, because he was in the room.
That Tom must have taken it before he left an hour earlier.

feedback.es: La segunda persona descarta a Tom porque se fue una hora antes; no acusa a Leo ni sostiene que Tom lo tomara antes de irse.

origin.audio: Two friends were discussing a missing wallet. The first said that Tom must have taken it, since he was the last person in the room. The second answered that it was Leo who had been there last, and added that Tom couldn't have taken it, because he had left an hour earlier. In the end, they agreed to ask both of them before saying anything to the others.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los hallazgos pueden indicar una conexión, pero no la prueban.»

answer.text: may

feedback.es: May + verbo base expresa cautela: los datos sugieren una conexión sin demostrarla.

origin.text: The study found a link between sleep and memory, but the authors are careful: they say that the findings ___ indicate a connection, not prove one.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Se podría sostener que hacen falta más pruebas.»

answer.text: It could be argued that more evidence is needed

feedback.es: It could be argued that + oración introduce una opinión con distancia académica, sin comprometerse del todo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué postura adopta el informe sobre la relación entre sueño y notas?

choices.text: It suggests that poor sleep is one cause among several.
It notes a link but avoids claiming a cause.
It warns that the survey is too small to show any link.

feedback.es: Señala que las notas fueron más bajas en ese grupo, pero «stop short of claiming» indica que evita afirmar una causa, sin hablar de varias causas ni del tamaño de la encuesta.

origin.text: The survey shows that seventy percent of students slept less than seven hours. The authors note that exam marks were lower in that group, but they stop short of claiming that poor sleep caused the drop.

prompt.es: Completa: «No puede haber ido al concierto, porque no tenía entrada.»

answer.text: can't

feedback.es: Can't have + participio expresa que algo es imposible en el pasado; aquí los datos (luz encendida, sin entrada) lo descartan.

origin.text: I am sure she was at home last night, because her light was on. She ___ have gone to the concert, since she had no ticket.

prompt.es: Reescribe con cautela: «The findings prove that homework harms sleep.»

answer.text: The findings may indicate that homework harms sleep.
accepted: The findings may indicate that homework harms sleep.
The findings could suggest that homework harms sleep.
The findings could indicate that homework harms sleep.
The findings might suggest that homework harms sleep.
The findings might indicate that homework harms sleep.
The findings may suggest that homework harms sleep.
The findings suggest that homework may harm sleep.
The findings indicate that homework may harm sleep.

feedback.es: Para matizar una afirmación se sustituye prove por indicate o suggest y se añade may, might o could.

origin.text: Afirmación rotunda: «The findings prove that homework harms sleep.» Reescríbela con cautela con un verbo modal y un verbo como indicate o suggest.

title.es: Analizar la letra de una canción original

es: Analizar el tema, el tono (incluidos los matices agridulces) y dos recursos figurados (símil, metáfora, personificación) en la letra de una canción original, leída y escuchada, e inferir qué efecto produce cada recurso.

teaching.en: This lyric is about the bus ride home at night, and its bittersweet mood comes from the contrast between the warm lights and the long, empty streets.
teaching.es: Esta letra trata del viaje a casa en autobús por la noche, y su ambiente agridulce nace del contraste entre las luces cálidas y las calles largas y vacías.
teaching.explanationEs: Lyric es el texto de una canción; bittersweet mezcla alegría y tristeza, y se explica con un contraste.
segments: This lyric is about the bus ride home at night, and its bittersweet mood
comes from the contrast between the warm lights and the long, empty streets.
teaching.audioText: This lyric is about the bus ride home at night, and its bittersweet mood comes from the contrast between the warm lights and the long, empty streets.

teaching.en: The theme is comfort: the singer wants to feel safe at home, although an undertone of tiredness suggests how long the day has been.
teaching.es: El tema es el consuelo: la cantante quiere sentirse segura en casa, aunque un matiz de cansancio sugiere lo largo que ha sido el día.
teaching.explanationEs: El tema es la idea central; el undertone es lo que se siente debajo, sin que la letra lo diga.
segments: The theme is comfort: the singer wants to feel safe at home,
although an undertone of tiredness suggests how long the day has been.
teaching.audioText: The theme is comfort: the singer wants to feel safe at home, although an undertone of tiredness suggests how long the day has been.

teaching.en: Each verse adds a detail about the journey, and the chorus repeats “take me home”, which makes that wish the emotional centre of the song.
teaching.es: Cada estrofa añade un detalle del viaje y el estribillo repite «llévame a casa», lo que convierte ese deseo en el centro emocional de la canción.
teaching.explanationEs: La repetición del estribillo subraya la idea principal; las estrofas la desarrollan.
segments: Each verse adds a detail about the journey, and the chorus repeats “take
me home”, which makes that wish the emotional centre of the song.
teaching.audioText: Each verse adds a detail about the journey, and the chorus repeats “take me home”, which makes that wish the emotional centre of the song.

teaching.en: “The city is a sleeping giant” is a metaphor, because it says that one thing is another without using like or as.
teaching.es: «La ciudad es un gigante dormido» es una metáfora, porque dice que una cosa es otra sin usar like ni as.
teaching.explanationEs: Metáfora: A es B, sin like ni as; aquí la ciudad parece enorme y tranquila.
segments: “The city is a sleeping giant” is a metaphor, because it
says that one thing is another without using like or as.
teaching.audioText: “The city is a sleeping giant” is a metaphor, because it says that one thing is another without using like or as.

teaching.en: “Like a paper boat on a slow, warm river” is a simile, and its tender image makes the singer sound small but calm.
teaching.es: «Como un barquito de papel en un río lento y cálido» es un símil, y su imagen tierna hace que la cantante parezca pequeña pero tranquila.
teaching.explanationEs: Símil: compara dos cosas con like o as; cada recurso produce un efecto, no solo decora.
segments: “Like a paper boat on a slow, warm river” is a simile,
and its tender image makes the singer sound small but calm.
teaching.audioText: “Like a paper boat on a slow, warm river” is a simile, and its tender image makes the singer sound small but calm.

teaching.en: The streetlamps whisper advice to the traveller, so the lyric uses personification to make the night sound friendly rather than frightening.
teaching.es: Las farolas susurran consejos al viajero, así que la letra usa personificación para que la noche suene amistosa y no aterradora.
teaching.explanationEs: Personificación: un objeto hace algo que solo hacen las personas; aquí cambia la sensación de la noche.
segments: The streetlamps whisper advice to the traveller, so the lyric uses
personification to make the night sound friendly rather than frightening.
teaching.audioText: The streetlamps whisper advice to the traveller, so the lyric uses personification to make the night sound friendly rather than frightening.

prompt.es: Lee la letra y elige cuál es su tema.

choices.text: Coming home safely after a long day.
Feeling lost in a city that is too big.
Waiting for a friend who is very late.

feedback.es: El estribillo repite «take me home» y el resto describe la ciudad de noche con calma: el tema es volver a casa con tranquilidad.

hint.es: Fíjate en el estribillo: Take me home.

origin.text: The city is a sleeping giant tonight, / and I am a small light moving through its dreams. / The streetlamps whisper, “Go slow, go slow.” / Take me home, take me home, / like a paper boat on a slow, warm river.

prompt.es: Elige qué recurso es «The streetlamps whisper».

choices.text: Metaphor: the lamps are said to be people.
Personification: lamps do something only people do.
Simile: the lamps are compared to people with like.

feedback.es: Las farolas no pueden susurrar: darles una acción humana es personificación, no metáfora ni símil.

hint.es: Las farolas hacen algo que solo hacen las personas.

prompt.es: Completa: «El estribillo repite el deseo principal de la canción.»

answer.text: chorus

feedback.es: El chorus es la parte que vuelve entre las estrofas y subraya la idea principal.

hint.es: Es la parte que vuelve entre una estrofa y otra.

origin.text: Each verse adds a new detail about the journey, while the ___ repeats the main wish of the song at the end of every section.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada verso con el recurso o el tono que transmite.

pairs: The moon is a silver plate.
The wind sings in the trees.

answer.text: It was raining when I reached the deserted station, and my bag was heavy. I had promised Sara that I would be there at eight, but the last train had already left. A man was sleeping on a bench, and a small clock was showing the wrong time above the ticket office. I felt cold and afraid. What I remember most is the silence, which was like a wall between me and the rest of the city. I took out my phone, but it had no power. Then I heard a voice behind me. It was my old teacher who was standing there with an umbrella! She had seen me from the bus and had followed me inside. She laughed, gave me her phone and said, “Call Sara. She has probably been waiting for you.” I called, and Sara answered at once. She was not angry. In fact, she had missed the train too, and she was waiting at the next station. We met her an hour later, and we laughed about the whole night. I will never forget how kind both of them were.
accepted: It was raining when I reached the deserted station, and my bag was heavy. I had promised Sara that I would be there at eight, but the last train had already left. A man was sleeping on a bench, and a small clock was showing the wrong time above the ticket office. I felt cold and afraid. What I remember most is the silence, which was like a wall between me and the rest of the city. I took out my phone, but it had no power. Then I heard a voice behind me. It was my old teacher who was standing there with an umbrella! She had seen me from the bus and had followed me inside. She laughed, gave me her phone and said, “Call Sara. She has probably been waiting for you.” I called, and Sara answered at once. She was not angry. In fact, she had missed the train too, and she was waiting at the next station. We met her an hour later, and we laughed about the whole night. I will never forget how kind both of them were.

It was getting dark when I arrived at the cinema, and a long line was waiting outside. I had bought the tickets two days before, but when I looked in my bag, I understood that I had left them at home. My heart was beating like a drum. What I felt most was shame, because Leo had already told everyone that the film was his idea. I walked to the desk and explained the problem. The woman smiled and said, “Do not worry. Show me the message on your phone.” I looked for it, but my hands were shaking. Finally I found it. It was a small miracle that the message was still there! She checked the name, printed two new tickets and wished us a good film. When I found Leo, the film had already started, so we sat in the dark and whispered like children. Afterwards we walked home and he laughed at me all the way. I remember that night as the day I learned to check my bag twice.

answer.text: Thank you, everyone. I'd like to propose a compromise: a small street market on the first Sunday of each month, with stalls for local food and plants.
